title: DomainConfig
description: Full configuration for one domain. One JSON file = one domain. Wire it in app/domains/index.ts — no other files need changing. INVARIANTS the engine relies on (not expressible in JSON Schema): (1) fillOrder must contain every entityTypes member — types missing from fillOrder are selected but silently omitted from the BOM. (2) Every non-anchor type belongs to exactly one fill group: selectionOrder (core types, with capacityType LAST) or postFillTypes — never both, or it gets filled twice. (3) aggregateDisplay.primary/safety must reference codes of check_type=aggregate rules only. (4) Every entity row must carry the costAttribute in its attributes; load/capacity/aggregate attributes must be numeric.

$schema.description: Points to this schema file for editor validation. Set to './schema.json'.

entityTypes.description: All entity type IDs in this domain. Used as the canonical list throughout the engine. Order does not matter here — use fillOrder and selectionOrder for ordering.

entityTypeLabels.description: Display names for each entity type. Keys must match entityTypes.

fillOrder.description: Order entity slots appear in the BOM output. MUST contain every entityTypes member — a type missing from fillOrder still gets selected but is silently omitted from the BOM. Also the fallback for selectionOrder (fillOrder minus anchorType) and the default for anchorType (first item) and capacityType (last item).

selectionOrder.description: Order the backtrack fill selects entities: core types first (filled share-by-share), then capacityType LAST. The fill picks the capacity unit last (cheapest adequate for the accumulated load) and stops there — any types listed after capacityType are never filled. Do NOT include anchorType (tried separately, before this order) or postFillTypes (filled in a later phase). Omit to use fillOrder minus anchorType.

maxPerType.description: Hard cap on quantity per entity type. Types not listed here default to 1 (or use dynamicMaxPerType). Use for types that are always a single unit.

dynamicMaxPerType.description: For entity types whose slot count depends on another entity's attribute (e.g., RAM slots from motherboard). Key = the entity type whose count is dynamic. Use {} if no dynamic types. Two shapes: sources+aggregate (multi-source) or formula (RuleFlow expr). WHO CONSUMES WHAT: the quantity cap (sources/formula/fallback) is enforced by the UI when the user pins items — the suggestion engine always fills quantity 1 per type and reads only sort_attribute and capacity_attribute, to rank candidates during selection.

requiredTypes.description: Entity types that must be present for a build to be valid. Missing types produce an error validation issue.

anchorType.description: The 'hero' entity that defines the tier of the whole build. The engine tries every anchor candidate and picks the best-fitting combination. Gets the largest share of the budget. If omitted, defaults to fillOrder[0].

capacityType.description: Entity type that acts as a capacity constraint (e.g., PSU for power). The engine selects the cheapest item whose capacityAttribute >= totalLoad / capacityFactor. If omitted, defaults to the LAST type in fillOrder — the capacity selection logic always applies to some type; there is no way to disable it. Must also appear as the last entry of selectionOrder. Requires capacityAttribute and loadAttributes.

capacityAttribute.description: Attribute on the capacityType entity that holds its rated capacity (e.g., watt_output for PSU). Required when capacityType is set.

loadAttributes.description: Attribute names representing load/consumption on non-capacity entities. The engine reads the first non-null attribute per entity (fallback chain). Required when capacityType is set.

capacityFactor.description: Safety multiplier for capacity selection. minCapacity = totalLoad / capacityFactor. 0.8 means the chosen unit must handle 125% of actual load (80% rule).

primary.description: Rule code to show as the main aggregate meter in the UI. Must match the code of a rule with check_type=aggregate — a pairwise rule code here breaks the meter.

safety.description: Rule code for the secondary safety meter (must also be an aggregate rule). Null to hide.

aggregateDisplay.description: Which aggregate rules to display as meters in the simulation UI.

costAttribute.description: Key in entity.attributes that holds the unit cost. The engine reads this for all budget calculations.

costColumn.description: Database column name for unit cost. Used in SQL queries (SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY). Must match the actual DB schema column.

costPrecision.description: Decimal places for cost display and rounding. 0 = whole numbers (THB), 2 = cents.

publishedStatus.description: The entity status value that means 'available for suggestion'. Only entities with this status are included in the pool.

fillStrategy.description: Name of the fill algorithm to use. Must match a registered strategy in app/engine/strategies/index.ts. Currently only 'backtrack' is available.

fetchLimits.description: How many DB rows to fetch per category. Higher values improve suggestion quality at the cost of more D1 row reads.

budgetPlan.description: RuleFlow2 module that calculates anchorTarget from effectiveBudget and entityCount. If omitted, uses: round(effectiveBudget * ceil(entityCount/2) / entityCount).

postFillTypes.description: Extra fill phases that run after backtrack fill completes. Use for entities selected in tiers (e.g., SSD: cheap first, upgrade later if budget allows).

tierRules.description: Cross-entity tier PREFERENCES (soft, not hard constraints). When a provider entity matches its condition, candidates of the required type that satisfy the condition are sorted first during selection — candidates that fail remain eligible and are still chosen when nothing tier-satisfying fits the budget. Use a pairwise rule instead if the combination must be blocked.

rules.description: All compatibility rules for this domain. Two check types: pairwise (entity vs entity) and aggregate (sum/count/min/max across types vs a capacity or fixed threshold). Aggregate rules are automatically skipped when no items of the target from_types are present in the build.

DynamicMaxCfg.description: Two shapes — sources+aggregate (multi-source lookup) or formula (RuleFlow expression). The computed max quantity caps UI pinning only; the suggestion engine fills quantity 1 per type and uses sort_attribute/capacity_attribute for candidate ranking.

DynMaxSources.description: Compute max quantity by reading one attribute per source entry, then combining all values with aggregate. Each entry in sources is intentionally one (entity_type, attribute) pair — add multiple entries to read from different types or different attributes on the same type.

sources.description: One entry = one (entity_type, attribute) pair. Missing entries (source entity not yet selected) are skipped — aggregate runs on whatever is available.

aggregate.description: How to combine the values read from all source entries. min = use the tightest constraint (most common), max = use the loosest, sum = add them together.

capacity_attribute.description: Attribute on the dynamic entity that counts how many slots one unit consumes (e.g., 'modules' for a dual-channel RAM kit).

sort_attribute.description: Attribute used to sort candidates during selection. Highest value preferred.

fallback.description: Max quantity to use when no source entity is selected yet.

DynMaxSourceEntry.description: One (entity_type, attribute) pair. Intentionally singular — source_type is a single string, not an array. To combine values from multiple types or multiple attributes on the same type, add separate entries to the sources array and let aggregate combine them.

source_type.description: The entity type to read from. Must be a key in entityTypes. Only the first selected item of this type is used.

source_attribute.description: The attribute name on that entity whose numeric value is used as the slot count contribution.

DynMaxFormula.description: Compute max quantity from a RuleFlow expression. Variables are auto-injected as {type}_{attribute} from all currently suggested entities.

formula.description: RuleFlow expression string. Variables are named {type}_{attribute} (e.g., $case_cpu_cooler_clearance_mm, $motherboard_vrm_height_mm). Built-in functions: round(x), ceil(x), floor(x), min(...), max(...), abs(x), clamp(x, lo, hi), pow(x, y), sqrt(x). Operators: + - * / % ** parentheses, comparisons == != > >= < <=, logic AND OR NOT. No ternary/if inside an expression.

capacity_attribute.description: Attribute on the dynamic entity that counts how many slots one unit consumes.

sort_attribute.description: Attribute used to sort candidates during selection. Highest value preferred.

fallback.description: Max quantity to use when formula throws or inputs are missing.

type.description: Entity type this phase applies to.

preferAttribute.description: Attribute to optimise for (highest value wins within budget).

maxAttrValue.description: Upper bound filter on preferAttribute (e.g., SSD ≤512 GB).

minAttrValue.description: Lower bound filter on preferAttribute (e.g., SSD ≥1000 GB).

upgradeExisting.description: false = initial fill of empty slot. true = replace existing item if budget allows a better option.

anchor.description: Max rows for anchorType (top-N by cost desc). Higher = wider anchor selection.

anchorNear.description: Extra rows for anchor fetched near the calculated anchorTarget price point.

core.description: Max rows per core entity type (top-N by cost desc).

coreCheap.description: Extra cheap rows per core entity type (top-N by cost asc).

name.description: Unique identifier for this tier rule.

entity_type.description: Entity type that triggers this rule when its condition matches.

condition.description: JSON Logic condition evaluated on the provider entity. Use { 'var': 'attributes.X' } to access attributes.

entity_type.description: Entity type this preference applies to when the provider matches.

condition.description: JSON Logic condition evaluated on each candidate. Satisfying candidates are preferred (sorted first); failing candidates are NOT excluded and may still be chosen.

id.description: Unique integer ID within this domain. Used as cache key — must not change once deployed.

code.description: Unique SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE code. Must match aggregateDisplay keys if used as a meter.

name.description: Human-readable rule name shown in error detail.

check_type.description: pairwise = evaluate one entity pair at a time. aggregate = sum/count across types vs a capacity.

severity.description: error = blocks valid build. warning = shown but does not block. info = informational.

priority.description: Evaluation order — higher number runs first.

is_active.description: Set false to disable without removing.

message.description: Failure message. Interpolation tokens — pairwise rules: :source.attributes.X, :target.attributes.X (also :source.name, :target.name); aggregate rules: :aggregate_value, :capacity_value, :utilization_pct. Tokens support pipe filters, e.g. ':aggregate_value | round(0)', ':source.name | upper' (see app/engine/template.ts for the full filter list).

resolution.description: Suggested fix shown to the user.

scope.description: Required for check_type=pairwise. Defines which entity pairs to evaluate.

condition.description: Pairwise: JSON Logic expression ({ '==': [...] }). Aggregate: object with top-level 'aggregate' key.

match_by.description: shared_attribute: same attribute key on both entities must match. attribute_pair: different keys on source vs target must match. attribute_range: source value must fall within target's range attribute.

attribute_key.description: shared_attribute only: the attribute key checked on both entities.

source_attribute.description: attribute_pair/range: attribute on the source entity.

target_attribute.description: attribute_pair/range: attribute on the target entity.

source_types.description: Restrict source to these entity types. Omit for all types.

target_types.description: Restrict target to these entity types.

JsonLogicCondition.description: JSON Logic expression. Must evaluate to true for the rule to pass. Operators: ==, !=, >, >=, <, <=, and, or, not, in, var. Access attributes with { 'var': 'source.attributes.X' } or { 'var': 'target.attributes.X' }. ARRAY SEMANTICS: when either side of == is an array, it passes if the scalar is contained in the array (or, for two arrays, if they intersect) — e.g. motherboard ram_type ['DDR4','DDR5'] == ram ram_type 'DDR4' passes. != is the negation (no containment/intersection). 'in' checks needle-in-haystack where haystack is an array.

AggregateCondition.description: Computes a value (sum/min/max/avg/count) across one or more entity types and compares it to a threshold. Threshold can be an entity attribute, a simulation constraint, or a fixed literal. The rule is automatically skipped when no items of the specified from_types are present. condition evaluates to true (= rule passes) when the comparison holds.

fallback_attributes.description: Try these if primary is null (e.g., ['tdp_w']).

from_types.description: Entity types to include. Use ['*'] for all types.

exclude_types.description: Entity types to exclude even if matched by from_types.

multiply_by_quantity.description: true = multiply attribute value by slot quantity (e.g., 2× RAM kits count double).

mode.description: entity_attribute: read capacity from an entity attribute. simulation_constraint: read from constraints map. fixed_value: literal number.

entity_type.description: entity_attribute mode: entity type that holds the capacity.

attribute.description: entity_attribute mode: attribute that holds the capacity value.

safety_factor.description: Multiply capacity by this before comparing (e.g., 0.8 for 80% rule).

constraint_key.description: simulation_constraint mode: key from the constraints map passed to validateItems.

value.description: fixed_value mode: compare against this literal number.

operator.description: aggregate_value operator capacity_value. Rule passes when this comparison is true.

Module.description: RuleFlow2 module for declarative formula evaluation. Used in budgetPlan to express anchor target calculation without hardcoded TypeScript.

inputs.description: Input variable declarations. All must be provided at runtime.

outputs.description: Output variable names. Must match the first element of each block's 'out' array.

blocks.description: Computation steps. Execution order follows data dependencies ($var references between blocks), not array order. Two block shapes: FormulaBlock (one expression → one output) and IfBlock (branch conditions → set several outputs).

name.description: Variable name — referenced in expr as $name.

Block.description: One computation step — either a formula block (single expression → one output) or an if block (conditional branches → one or more outputs).

IfBlock.description: Conditional block. Execution: (1) every output in outs is first set to its fallback, (2) branch conditions are evaluated top-to-bottom and the FIRST matching branch applies its payload and stops, (3) if no branch matches, the else payload applies. Outputs a payload does not set keep their fallback value.

outs.description: Outputs this block owns. Payload keys must be declared here.

else.description: Payload applied when no branch condition matches.

prefixItems.description: Fallback value, assigned before any branch runs.
Condition expression — same grammar as formula expr (e.g. '$effectiveBudget >= 80000 AND $entityCount > 4').

oneOf.description: Set map — keys must be outputs declared in the block's outs. A string value is parsed as an expression when it parses (e.g. '$budget / 2'); otherwise it is kept as a string literal.

Payload.description: What a branch (or else) does: either set declared outputs directly, or run nested blocks.

FormulaBlock.description: A single formula step. Output can be referenced by subsequent blocks.

expr.description: Expression string. Reference variables with $name. Built-in functions: round(x), ceil(x), floor(x), min(...), max(...), abs(x), clamp(x, lo, hi), pow(x, y), sqrt(x). Operators: + - * / % ** parentheses, comparisons == != > >= < <=, logic AND OR NOT. No ternary/if inside an expression.
